messages:
Jun: heads-up — after the autoscale yesterday we saw a sustained p95 latency jump (~120ms -> ~230ms) and a big drop in prefix cache hit-rate.
Jun: trending numbers: runtime.prefix_cache.hitrate went from ~78% before scale to ~21% after scale; token cost per request up by ~14%.
Jun: logs show a lot of cache.populate events with 0 keys inserted: `cache.populate keys=0 reason=key_mismatch` — odd.
Priya: @Jun thanks — did you correlate with the 21:00 deploy? deploy-bot reported canary successful.
Priya: quick checked CI change: we switched to hashed_prompt_v2 keying in the model-serving layer in that deploy. That changes the key delimiter and drops some normalization steps.
Priya: example old vs new:
```
old: prefix_key:text|len=64|norm=lower
new: hpv2:sha256:0x9ab3f4
```
Priya: if warmers are still priming using the old format they won't match — explains keys=0.
Mateo: that aligns with perf profile I pulled earlier: after scale most traffic hit cold KV paths and kernel-selection time is amortized badly when KV miss-rate spikes.
Mateo: sample profile snippet (wall ms per request): `kv_lookup  -> 58ms, kernel_select -> 12ms, decode -> 82ms` when hit-rate low. When hit-rate high kv_lookup -> 6ms.
Alex: immediate mitigation: we can toggle the feature flag to keep old keying on the canary fraction and trigger a targeted backfill.
Alex: also recommend adding an autoscaler hook: on node add, call warmers for that node's model set (helps avoid blast of misses). Right now autoscaler only signals prometheus and doesn't call warmers.
Samira: agreed. Proposed immediate action plan:
1) rollback hashed_prompt_v2 flag for canary and pause rollout (toggle = off).
2) run a cross-zone synthetic prefill job that replays top-10k prefixes for the affected model versions (synthetic warmers) — schedule once per 30m for 3 hours.
3) add autoscale-on-up hook that invokes `POST /internal/warmers/seed?node=$NODE&model=$MODEL`.
4) instrument a metric `runtime.warmers.fill_rate` and add alert if it drops >30% vs baseline.
Samira: sample job command for the prefill:
```
curl -XPOST https://internal.redwood/warmers/seed \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WARMERS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-1","prefix_set":"top10k","rate":200}'
```
Priya: good. one more note — hashed_prompt_v2 de-duplicates similar prompts which improves cache density long-term, so we want it, but need a migration strategy (backfill + dual-key lookup window) rather than flip-and-forget.
Priya: suggestion: add dual-lookup logic for 48h where we check new key then fallback to legacy key before creating populate entries.
Mateo: can add that as a short-lived shim in runtime — low-risk and buys time for backfill to populate the v2 keys.
Alex: ops steps I will run now: roll canary flag off, trigger immediate prefill job for the canary pool, and add temporary alert for prefix_cache.hitrate < 50%.
Alex: also scheduling a postmortem thread if anything else pops up.
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: warmers job queued for pool canary-eu-west (job id w-20260318-431)
deploy-bot: :rocket: autoscaler hook merge request opened: github.com/redwood/infra/merge/512
Jun: thanks team. after we stabilize let's add a regression test in perf harness that simulates scale-up and verifies hit-rate recovers within N minutes.
Samira: will own the playbook update and add the cron for the scheduled cross-zone prefill: `0 */2 * * *` (every 2 hours) — but we'll keep it disabled by default until we have safeguards.
Jun: filing follow-ups: track PBs for (a) dual-lookup shim, (b) autoscaler hook, (c) scheduled prefill job + throttling, (d) perf regression test.
Jun: if anyone has logs/traces from the 21:00->21:45 window please paste them here or attach — they help quantify backfill progress.
Mateo: attaching a short flamegraph link in thread: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/abcd1234 — shows kv stalls at scale-up.
Priya: will draft migration doc for hashed_prompt_v2 and propose rollout steps (backfill window, dual-lookup, feature-flag gating).
Alex: long-term we should also consider making warmers idempotent and able to accept bulk key lists produced from offline freq analysis — less runtime churn.
Samira: noted. creating a checklist item in the playbook for idempotent warmers + bulk ingest.
Jun: thanks all — feel better about path forward. :thumbsup
